tasks.spec:
You are closing review findings on a text-message appointment-recall pathway you previously built. A senior reviewer returned REVISE. Your current working directory IS a disposable git worktree containing your previous build. Revise it in place; do not start over.

BOUNDARY.
- You own exactly three files and may modify NOTHING else: scripts/build_v22_recall_map.py, scripts/validate_v22.py, tests/test_v22_scenarios.py. You may also write generated output under build/.
- NEVER run git commit, git push, or any git write command. Leave changes uncommitted.
- NEVER call a network endpoint. NEVER load skills, call MCP tools or Apps, or capture notes to any external memory.
- Do not modify anything under contract/.

READ FIRST: contract/state-procedure-map.md. It has been AMENDED since your build, and the amendments are listed at the bottom of it. The reviewer found three defects in the map itself, not just in your graph, and the map now carries new rules R4a, R10 and R11 plus a widened R8. contract/review-v22.json holds the full verdict with all ten findings.

THE FIXES. All are mandatory. Five of them are already enforced by the orchestrator gate that will run against your output, so you can verify each one yourself.

1. R4a, HIGH. Silence after a booking is success, not a no-reply. n_confirm currently routes its 72-hour timeout to e_timeout. Most patients who receive "you are booked" never reply, so the ordinary success path records no_reply and the booking rate reads near zero while bookings are actually happening. Route n_confirm's timeout edge to e_booked instead. Only n_offer and n_negotiate route their timeout to e_timeout.

2. R8 widened, HIGH. e_stop's patient-facing text currently says the patient is opted out and that no more messages will be sent. Nothing in the system can keep that promise, because no suppression store exists and the next campaign can text them again. No text, name, outcome, tag or global label on e_stop or e_not_me may assert that a number was opted out, suppressed, removed from a list, unsubscribed, or will not receive further messages. Acknowledge the request and route it to a human: the office can honour it, the graph cannot. Rewrite both messages accordingly.

3. R10, MEDIUM. n_availability and n_search route slot_count with a bare complement, so a gateway response reporting three or more openings falls to n_negotiate, whose only situational instruction is that no openings are available. Add an explicit >= route covering two or more, and make sure the node each count lands on is written for that case.

4. R11, MEDIUM. n_identity compares patient_id against the template {{recall_patient_id}}. Whether the platform interpolates a template on the right-hand side of a routing condition is unproven, and a guard that silently never fires is worse than no guard. Replace it with a comparison against something the response itself provides, such as the match count.

5. R6 clarified, MEDIUM. The offer prompt tells the model to send a template verbatim AND to render each start time for display. Those contradict each other, because rendering the time is precisely a change to the template. A live test showed the model resolving the contradiction by shipping the raw timestamp. State the rule once: the wording is fixed, and each slot start placeholder is replaced by that time rendered as a weekday, date and clock time in America/New_York. Do not use the word verbatim.

6. MEDIUM. The offer prompt never says that when only one opening exists there is no second opening to select, while the edge to the second verify node exists regardless of count. Say it explicitly, so a patient who earlier saw two openings and then receives a fresh single-slot offer cannot select a stale second one.

7. LOW, test honesty. Two tests promise more than they check. One claims prompts never assign calendar work to the model but only greps for two phrases. One claims a decline never reaches the opt-out exit but only checks static edges, when both are globals selected at runtime from their labels. Either narrow the test names to what is actually asserted, or strengthen the assertions to match the names. Do not leave a test whose name overstates its coverage.

INVARIANTS THAT DO NOT CHANGE. Every comparison value is a string literal, never a boolean or integer. Every silent step keeps a != complement, and no verify node puts that complement on a booking node. No node attaches a tool. Every webhook uses the stored secret reference with retryAttempts 0. Booking is /sign only with verb appt.book and reason new-booking and no allow_conflict. n_identity is the only start node. Confirmation is reachable only on a booking success. n_faq is the only auto-returning global. Nothing may claim a suppression. Ceilings stay 24 nodes and 52 edges.

HOW TO VERIFY, from the worktree root:
  mkdir -p build
  python3 scripts/build_v22_recall_map.py --out build/v22_a.json
  python3 scripts/build_v22_recall_map.py --out build/v22_b.json
  diff build/v22_a.json build/v22_b.json
  python3 scripts/validate_v22.py
  python3 -m pytest tests/test_v22_scenarios.py -q

All five must succeed, and the orchestrator gate enforces every fix above by rule number.

HARD RULES. Do not weaken a safety invariant to close a finding. Do not write a test that asserts a property its own helper injects. Do not commit.
tasks.verified: all seven review findings are closed and the graph passes the amended gate, including booked-and-silent routing to the booked exit, no false suppression promise in patient-facing text, explicit multi-opening routing, and no template used as a comparison value
